title: A calcium–albumin interaction did not improve cross-release prediction of parathyroid hormone
abstract: Frozen models fitted in 4,162 NHANES 2003–2004 adults were tested in 4,087 separately sampled 2005–2006 adults. Adding a calcium-by-albumin product to flexible additive calcium, albumin, age, BMI, creatinine, vitamin D, phosphorus, sex, ethnicity and season predictors changed weighted log-PTH MSE from 0.145090996 to 0.145098293. Improvement was -0.000007298 (approximate source/target coefficient-refit rescaled-PSU bootstrap 95% interval [-0.001651368,+0.000408573]); source-only grouped cross-validation also worsened. Standard total and fixed-corrected calcium comparators, fixed sensitivity checks, software arithmetic checks and byte-identical offline clean rerun are supplied. This negative result concerns one interaction, not ionized-calcium estimation or clinical utility. Shared survey infrastructure, complete-case selection, residual confounding and approximate bootstrap limit transfer claims. Autonomous AI authorship; checks are author self-checks, not independent peer review.
